content: WXT's built-in wxt:locationchange event is powered by polling location every ~1s (wxt-dev/wxt issue 1567), so it is slow. That issue states plainly: 'This doesn't work in isolated content scripts. history.pushState in the content script is not the same function as history.pushState in the main world.' - i.e. an isolated-world history monkeypatch cannot see the page's own navigations. The proposed fix is to inject a MAIN-world script that patches pushState/replaceState and listens to popstate. Navigation API: each window has its own navigation instance and the navigate event fires for all navigation types, but behaviour across extension isolated worlds is not documented.
